title: Eyewitness Testimony: The Cognitive Interview
welcome_lead: Four steps from Geiselman that beat the standard police interview.
meta_desc: A-Level Psychology Cognitive Interview Geiselman four techniques effectiveness.
final_note: Cued recall + multiple perspectives = more accurate testimony.

walkthroughs.body_html: Geiselman et al. (1985) built the CI on memory theory: encoding specificity (reinstate context, change perspective) and multiple traces (report everything, reverse order). Each technique probes different cues to overcome retrieval failure.

Kohnken et al. (1999) meta-analysed 53 studies: the CI produced 34% more correct information than standard interviews. Errors were slightly higher, but the cost-benefit favoured the CI for serious crime. Mello & Fisher (1996): the CI is especially effective with older witnesses.

The CI takes longer and demands trained interviewers — UK police rarely use the full version. Fisher et al. (1987) Enhanced CI adds rapport, open questioning and minimisation of interruptions. Kebbell (1999): only 3% of UK officers used all four CI techniques.
